Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket visibly closed more than in the input image, with its front panels brought together at least in part?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows the jacket's front panels brought together along some portion of the closure compared with the input. Fail if the jacket is visibly unchanged or more open. Unknown if the closure cannot be assessed from the image or comparison evidence is insufficient.
node.binding: Assess only the woman's jacket identified in the input image; judge visible change to its front closure, not unrelated edits.

node_traces.evidence: The jacket’s front is visibly more open in the edited image, with a panel hanging away from her body, rather than brought together compared with the source.

fulfillment: The node is structurally valid and its checks were queried successfully, so this is not a transport or schema failure. The disagreement is in the visual evidence: the edited image shows the woman turned sideways with the jacket front/panel hanging away from her body, while the source also appears open; the traces therefore do not establish closure or progress toward it. Do not force the reference label to yes. Improve the typed checks so they compare the same jacket closure in source and edit, distinguish a changed viewpoint or swinging panel from actual closure progress, and assess whether an opening remains along the front. Keep complete, partial, absent, and unknown distinct: use unknown if pose, occlusion, or image quality prevents a reliable comparison, rather than treating uncertainty as failure. The repeated high-confidence fail traces are consistent with the visible edit, not evidence that the requested change is absent from the node’s criteria.
s2: The node is valid and successfully queried, so this is not a transport or schema issue. Its endpoint criterion is appropriate, but the binding should explicitly compare the same jacket’s closure in source and edit while accounting for the changed pose and viewpoint. The edited image shows the woman turned sideways and the jacket panel swinging away; that alone does not establish whether closure progressed, and the source is also difficult to assess. Keep complete closure distinct from partial progress and no progress, and return unknown when the closure cannot be reliably inspected rather than inferring failure from the panel’s position. Do not tune the criterion to force the reference label: the label constrains the aggregate but is not atomic visual ground truth.
